scenes.title: Prologue — The Hive, remembered
scenes.prose: Night. Rain. An eleven-storey block of balconies and wires wedged between glass towers.

dialogueBeats.text: This is how I remember it.

captions.text: This is how I remember it.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: After the war they raised a block beside the railway, to house the factories.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: The factories closed. We stayed.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: We built upward. A room for a daughter. A shop for a brother.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: A stair, a pipe, a balcony bolted onto a balcony.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: Sixty years, until nobody could say where the factory ended and we began.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: The city grew up around us, and forgot we were here.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: That was all right. We were busy.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: Now the land is worth more than we are. Everything is going.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

captions.text: We are just slower.
captions.speaker: KANEKO

scenes.title: 1 — The backstreet

dialogueBeats.text: Rain. Not a storm. Just cold, steady, patient rain.
A vending machine hums on the corner. High up, one lit window, a radio playing behind it.
MARA VOSS (24) walks fast, arms folded, soaked, no umbrella.
Her phone lights up: VERA. She watches it ring.

captions.text: Not tonight.
captions.speaker: MARA

dialogueBeats.text: She declines it.

THE SCRAP

The note in her hands. Her handwriting, in biro: 1.00 Sakai. Underneath is an address. Beneath that, underlined twice: "just listen."
She looks down the lane. At the far end, the bar sign. She checks her watch (12.45). Early.
The rain thickens.
The beer crates will hide her from anyone in the lane. She hopes. She isn't sure she wants to walk in at all.
Somewhere nearby, a pedestrian crossing CHIMES its old melody for an empty intersection. Over and over. No one crosses.
An OLD MAN (70s) in a cheap raincoat and a grey flat cap comes in from the road, one hand pressed to his side as if something is hidden there.
She leans out of the shadow. The red bird clip catches the street light.
He sees it. He stops, six metres short of her. For one second his whole face changes.
Then he shakes his head. Barely.
A man refusing a stranger.
And he turns his back on her, slowly, to face the road.
Behind him, at the mouth of the lane, headlights. A black sedan pulls across the opening and stops, blocking it.
Its high beams shine straight down the lane, lighting the rain in long white columns.
Two MEN get out and walk in, black silhouettes against the glare. Black clothes. Masks. They don't run.
The old man doesn't move.
After twenty years.
A suppressed SHOT.
Flat and ordinary, like a door closing.
One of the masked men touches his ear.

captions.text: First position done. Moving to second.
captions.speaker: MASKED MAN

dialogueBeats.text: They walk back to the sedan. They don't hurry. They never look at the doorway.
It pulls away and takes the long way round the block, its high beams swinging off the lane.
Mara runs to the old man. Her bag slides off her shoulder and spills across the wet street. She doesn't notice.

captions.text: Mr. Sakai?
captions.speaker: MARA

captions.text: Hold on, I'll call an ambulance.
captions.speaker: MARA

dialogueBeats.text: His hand comes out of his coat with something small and brass in it. He presses it into her palm and closes her fingers over it.

captions.text: Don't let them have it.
captions.speaker: OLD MAN

captions.text: Have what? I don't —
captions.speaker: MARA

dialogueBeats.text: In her hand: a small brass key on a stamped number tag.
On the pavement: a puddle of rainwater, leaking blood.
At the other end of the street, the amber glow of a bar. Mara runs for it.
Behind her, on the street: her purse, open in the rain.

scenes.title: 2 — The small bar

dialogueBeats.text: Six stools and a counter. Shelves of bottles glowing amber.
Mara bursts in, the key in her fist.

captions.text: Miss Voss?
captions.speaker: JOURNALIST

dialogueBeats.text: He knows her name.

captions.text: Are you okay? Where's Sakai?
captions.speaker: JOURNALIST

dialogueBeats.text: Before she can answer, the door opens behind her. Rain noise.

captions.text: Shitsurei shimasu. (Excuse me.)
captions.speaker: MASKED MAN

dialogueBeats.text: Mara is behind the counter before she knows she's moved.
Two men in masks, inside the door. The journalist doesn't get up.
Two shots.
Behind the counter, Mara folds herself into the gap between the crates and the ice bin.

captions.text: Second position done.
captions.speaker: MASKED MAN

dialogueBeats.text: He takes one step toward the counter. A voice in his earpiece: one word. He turns and goes.
The door swings shut. The television laughs again.

scenes.title: 3 — Three days later

dialogueBeats.text: THREE DAYS LATER
An old four-story apartment block squeezed between newer buildings.
Laundry left out on a balcony, getting rained on.
A train slides past on the elevated line behind it, windows lit, and the whole building trembles faintly.
One window on the third floor is lit.

scenes.title: 4 — Vera's apartment

dialogueBeats.text: Small and tidy. Grey light through rain-streaked glass. A smartphone on the table; an old boxy television in the corner.
By the door, in the umbrella stand: a pale blue umbrella. Bone dry.
On a shelf, one framed photograph, its colors gone warm and faded. A Tokyo street, twenty years ago.
Behind them, the sign of a noodle shop.
VERA VOSS (29) sits at the low table.
Two cups. Hers holds cold tea.
The other is empty and clean, set out as though someone is expected.
It's Mara. You know what to do.

captions.text: It's Mara. You know what to do.
captions.speaker: MARA

dialogueBeats.text: Vera opens her mouth. For a moment, nothing.
It's me again. I'm not angry anymore. I wasn't really angry then, either. Whatever that man wants, it doesn't matter.

captions.text: It's me again. I'm not angry anymore.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I wasn't really angry then, either.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Whatever that man wants, it doesn't matter.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I just — You left your umbrella. You'll get soaked.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Just call me. You don't have to say anything. Just call, so I know.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: The old television murmurs to itself.

captions.text: ...police in Kanda are investigating a double
captions.speaker: NEWS REPORTER

captions.text: shooting in a small bar in the early hours of Sunday.
captions.speaker: NEWS REPORTER

captions.text: Two men were killed.
captions.speaker: NEWS REPORTER

captions.text: Officers say it appears to be a dispute between criminal groups.
captions.speaker: NEWS REPORTER

captions.text: No arrests have been made...
captions.speaker: NEWS REPORTER

dialogueBeats.text: ...rain continuing through the rest of the week...
She looks at the umbrella by the door. At the clean, empty cup. At the photograph.
She stands. Puts on her coat. Hesitates at the door.
Then she takes the blue umbrella. Mara's umbrella.

scenes.title: 5 — The front counter
scenes.prose: INT. POLICE STATION, FRONT COUNTER - NIGHT

dialogueBeats.text: Fluorescent tubes, one of them flickering. A long counter. Faded posters about pickpockets and traffic safety.
Vera stands at the counter, the closed blue umbrella dripping onto the linoleum.
A YOUNG OFFICER takes her details with polite boredom.

captions.text: Your sister's age?
captions.speaker: YOUNG OFFICER

captions.text: Twenty-four.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Adults sometimes go away for a few days. Especially foreigners.
captions.speaker: YOUNG OFFICER

captions.text: It's usually —
captions.speaker: YOUNG OFFICER

captions.text: She doesn't. Not without telling me.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: He types the name. ON THE MONITOR: MARA VOSS.
He looks at the screen a moment too long. Then he picks up the desk phone and turns away from her.
Yes. That name. Yes — the sister is here now.
He hangs up. His manner has changed. Politer.
Someone will be right with you.
Vera looks at him. He doesn't meet her eyes.

scenes.title: 6 — The interview room
scenes.prose: INT. POLICE STATION, INTERVIEW ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

dialogueBeats.text: Small. A table, two chairs, a box of tissues nobody has touched in years. Rain on a frosted window.
DETECTIVE ISHIDA (50s) sets a paper cup of tea in front of Vera. Gentle. Unhurried. Tired, in a way that looks like decency.
You must be cold.
His English is excellent.
I speak Japanese.

captions.text: I speak Japanese.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Of course. But this is a difficult thing.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: It is easier in your own language.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: The officer made a phone call the moment he had my sister's name.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Then you came.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: A foreign passport. We like to take care with these things.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: He slides a form across the table, and a pen. MISSING PERSON, in Japanese, with an English line beneath.
Name. Height. What she was wearing, if you know.
She fills it in. Her handwriting is fast and square. Ishida reads it upside down as she writes, without seeming to.

captions.text: Voss. You grew up here?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Until I was nine.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: And your parents? They are in America?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: My mother is. My father died.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Here?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Here. When I was a child.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I'm sorry. Did your sister ever talk about him?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: The pen stops.

captions.text: She was four. She doesn't remember him.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: A recent photograph?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Vera takes her wallet from her bag.

captions.text: She gave me two when she renewed. In case.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: In case.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: He takes it by the edges. Looks at it a moment. Sets it on the form, squares it to the corner.

captions.text: When did you last see her?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Thursday. At my apartment. We had dinner.
And how did she seem?
Vera hesitates.

captions.text: Normal.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: Ishida waits, kindly, as if he knows there is more. She doesn't give it.

captions.text: Did she ever speak of your family?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Anything she had been thinking about?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: No.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Did she mention Kanda? Friends there? Work?
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Kanda? No. Why —

captions.text: Kanda? No. Why —
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: The shootings. In Kanda. It was on the news.

captions.text: The shootings. In Kanda. It was on the news.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Is she hurt?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: We have no reason to believe she is hurt.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: That's not the same as saying she isn't.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Miss Voss —
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Is she dead?

captions.text: Is she dead?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: We have no reason to believe so.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Stop saying that.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Stop saying what you have no reason to believe and tell me what you know.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: The cup crumples in her fist. Hot tea runs over her fingers and onto the table, across the corner of the form. She doesn't seem to feel it.

What I know is that two men were killed in Kanda, and that it is a matter between criminal groups. And that your sister is a young woman who has not called her sister for three days. Those may be two separate things.

captions.text: What I know is that two men were killed in Kanda,
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: and that it is a matter between criminal groups.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: And that your sister is a young woman who has not called her sister for three days.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Those may be two separate things.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: May be.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: May be.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: She is my sister. I have been calling her for days. If you know where she is, tell me.

captions.text: She is my sister. I have been calling her for days.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: If you know where she is, tell me.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I do not know where she is. That is the truth.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: And if, on the off chance, she did see something she should not have,
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Silence. Rain on the frosted window.

captions.text: Go home, Miss Voss. Keep your phone on. If she calls, call me first.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Any hour.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: He slides his card across the wet table. She looks at it. Then takes it. Stands. Picks up the blue umbrella.

captions.text: You would have told me if she was dead. Wouldn't you?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Of course, I'm sure we will find her, you have my word.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Ishida sits alone a moment. He wipes the spilled tea from the table with the tissue, slowly, carefully, until there is no trace of it.
Then he picks up the passport photo, dry at the edges, looks at Mara's face, and slides it into his inside pocket.

scenes.title: 7 — The detectives' room
scenes.prose: INT. POLICE STATION, DETECTIVES' ROOM - CONTINUOUS

dialogueBeats.text: Rows of cluttered desks under humming fluorescent light. Most are empty at this hour. A radio plays low somewhere.
Ishida sits at his desk and opens the bottom drawer. The two drawers above it stay closed.

THE DRAWER

Inside the drawer, sealed together in one clear evidence bag: Mara's purse and the torn strap, coiled beside it. Still damp.
He looks at it a long moment.
Closes the drawer.
On the wall, the clock runs a minute fast.

scenes.title: 8 — We're closed

dialogueBeats.text: The same bar in flat grey daylight. It looks smaller without the night. Chairs up on the counter. The CRT television is dark.

captions.text: We're closed.
captions.speaker: OKADA

dialogueBeats.text: My sister. Four nights ago. Was she here?
Okada looks at the photo for exactly one second.

captions.text: No.
captions.speaker: OKADA

captions.text: You didn't look.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I looked. No.
captions.speaker: OKADA

dialogueBeats.text: His eyes go, just once, to the far end of the counter. Then back to the mop.
She has left the blue umbrella leaning against a stool.

scenes.title: 9 — Behind the counter

dialogueBeats.text: Rain. Vera walks away down the narrow street, no umbrella, head down.

captions.text: Miss.
captions.speaker: OKADA

dialogueBeats.text: He hands it to her. Then he holds out his other hand. In it: the small red enamel bird clip.
It was mine. She took it when we were kids. She never gave it back.

captions.text: It was mine. She took it when we were kids. She never gave it back.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Behind the counter. After.
captions.speaker: OKADA

captions.text: Did you give this to the police?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: They didn't ask.
captions.speaker: OKADA

dialogueBeats.text: He takes a business card from his apron and presses it into her hand. Old, soft at the corners, handwritten on the back.

captions.text: Not the police. Him.
captions.speaker: OKADA

captions.text: Who is he?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: He found my daughter once. When no one else would look.
captions.speaker: OKADA

dialogueBeats.text: Vera looks at the card. Printed in English and in katakana: JACK. INVESTIGATIONS. An address. No surname.

scenes.title: 10 — Depends who's calling

dialogueBeats.text: Second floor of an old building pressed against the elevated railway. One room.
JACK (48) sits at the desk eating a convenience-store rice ball, watching the silent swordsmen.
A knock on the frosted glass. Vera comes in, wet, the blue umbrella dripping.

captions.text: Are you the one they call Jack?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Depends who's calling.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Mr. Okada. The bar in Kanda.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Sit down.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: My sister has been missing for four days. The police say to go home and wait.

captions.text: My sister has been missing for four days.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: The police say to go home and wait.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I don't do missing persons. People who go missing usually want to.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: She places the red bird clip on his desk.

captions.text: She was in that bar. The night two men were shot there.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: What did the police tell you?
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: To go home.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: It's good advice.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Is it yours, too?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Do you have photographs of her?
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: The old framed photograph from her shelf, taken out of its frame. Twenty years ago. The American man in the rumpled suit.

captions.text: That's us. Before we left.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Your father.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: He died. That year. Here.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: Jack picks the photograph up by its edges, carefully, the way you'd handle evidence. Or something fragile.
He looks a moment too long at the noodle shop sign. Then he sets it down, face up, and squares it to the edge of the desk.
I'm sorry.

captions.text: I'm sorry.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: It was a long time ago.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Yes.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Ten thousand yen a day. Plus expenses.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: I'll need a key to her apartment, her phone number,
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: her friends, where she worked, where she drank.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: So you'll look.

captions.text: So you'll look.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I'll look.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: Mr. Okada said you found his daughter.

captions.text: Mr. Okada said you found his daughter.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I found her.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Was she alive?
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Her Japanese. Your sister's. Is it good?
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Some. Badly.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Then she stands out. That helps.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: Vera nods. Goes. Through the frosted glass, her shape goes down the stairs and is gone.

scenes.title: 11 — Two men laughing

dialogueBeats.text: Past midnight. Only the desk lamp and the grey flicker of the television, now showing static.

THE CLIPPING

An English-language newspaper, yellowed. A small headline: AMERICAN INSURANCE INVESTIGATOR FOUND DEAD - POLICE RULE SUICIDE.
A photograph: the same man from Vera's picture. The caption: DANIEL VOSS, 41.
Beneath the clipping, one more photograph.
Jack looks at it for a long time.
Then he dials the rotary phone. It takes a long time to dial.

captions.text: It's late, Jack.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: The Voss girl came to see me.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: I know.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Her sister was in that bar.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: The sister is a missing persons case. The bar is a gang matter.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Two separate things.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: And the old man in the street?
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Sakai. Yes. That Sakai. I know what you're thinking.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

captions.text: Old debts, old enemies. It's a gang matter.
captions.speaker: ISHIDA

dialogueBeats.text: Twenty years, Ishida.

captions.text: Twenty years, Ishida.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: Go to sleep, Jack. You found enough twenty years ago. You're too old to be haunted.
Jack holds the receiver a moment longer. He sets it down.
Flicks the lighter open. Shut.

scenes.title: 12 — The strap

dialogueBeats.text: The street from the cold open. The rain hasn't stopped in four days.

captions.text: Thank you
captions.speaker: VENDING MACHINE

captions.text: very much.
captions.speaker: VENDING MACHINE

dialogueBeats.text: Caught on a rough metal edge at knee height: a short twist of torn leather strap.
He doesn't touch it. He looks from the strap, to the spot where Sakai fell, to the bar sign. Reconstructing it.
A shutter RATTLES up above him. A BARBER (80s), in pajamas, looks down from the upstairs window.

captions.text: Police again?
captions.speaker: BARBER

captions.text: Not for a long time.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: I told them. I was asleep. I heard the shot. Then a car.
captions.speaker: BARBER

captions.text: One car?
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: One car. Twice. It left. Then it came back.

captions.text: One car. Twice. It left. Then it came back.
captions.speaker: BARBER

captions.text: Why come back?
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: Nobody answers. He looks down the street at the drains, the doorways, the gutter: everywhere a small thing could fall.
Jack drops the unopened coffee into the recycling bin. The can CLANKS. The crossing melody starts up somewhere, for no one.

scenes.title: 14 — Someone who meant to come back

dialogueBeats.text: A tiny studio in an old building. Grey daylight. Clothes on every surface. Sketches taped to the walls: pencil, charcoal, cheap watercolour.

captions.text: When were you last here?
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: A week ago. She made me coffee. It was terrible.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: Jack opens the fridge. Milk. A half-eaten cake in a box. He closes it.

captions.text: She wasn't planning to disappear.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: No.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: He crouches by the futon. A suitcase underneath, packed and zipped. He looks at it, then at Vera.

captions.text: That was for America. She'd booked a flight. Next month.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: You didn't want her to go.
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: I didn't want her to run away again. That's what I said.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: The night she left. That she always runs.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: She looks at the wall of drawings, not at him.
It was about Dad. It's always about Dad. She wanted to dig it all up. Who he was here. Why he — I told her to leave him dead. She said I was the one who ran.

captions.text: It was about Dad. It's always about Dad.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: She wanted to dig it all up. Who he was here.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Why he — I told her to leave him dead.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: She said I was the one who ran.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: All the way back here, chasing a ghost, and I won't even look at it.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: I told her to go, then. Go home.
captions.speaker: VERA

captions.text: Those were the last things I said to her.
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: Page after page of the same place. A tiny noodle counter under a railway. Six stools. A curtain. A hand-painted sign.

captions.text: She drew this a lot.
captions.speaker: JACK

dialogueBeats.text: Since she was little. It's from a story I used to tell her. About the noodle shop Dad took us to. She was too young to remember it, so I told her. She made it up from what I said. It's not real.
Jack turns a page. The sign, in careful ink. Every stroke of the kanji correct.
Can I borrow this?

captions.text: Can I borrow this?
captions.speaker: JACK

captions.text: Why?
captions.speaker: VERA

dialogueBeats.text: Vera takes the hair clip out of her coat pocket and sets it on the sketchbook.

captions.text: Take this too. It's mine. She stole it.
captions.speaker: VERA
